need: Teams larger than a few people drift on what shared terms mean, receive review findings without the rule they rest on, repeat the same review comment instead of turning it into a check, and design changes in unfamiliar code before tracing how a real request flows through it.
evidence: The decision owner reviewed public talks on team-scale engineering practice and public browser-vendor guidance for coding agents, and approved adapting their practice-level ideas: a shared glossary, separate spec and standards review conclusions, recurring review comments turned into checks, a periodic module depth check, tracing one vertical slice, short local instructions with a trigger, quoting the governing rule, quiet advisory checks and opt-in gates an agent cannot pass.
limits: Adapted ideas, not observations measured in the adopting project. Guidance only: no checker rule or record schema changes, and tests do not establish that agents obey prose. Each sentence and the glossary template were written for the kit; no text, code or example was copied from any source.
sanitization: Removed project names, task identifiers, links to the reviewed sources' threads and paths. No credentials, private account data, employer, client or third-party text is included.
